findings.evidence: "Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email."
findings.fix: Replace with a clear statement of the normal approval timeline and escalation process when the manager is unavailable.
findings.location: How to Apply section, third paragraph
findings.violation: This sentence describes a specific operational problem rather than the standard procedure. It reads like a bug report or incident description, not a policy instruction.

findings.evidence: "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.fix: Choose one approach and state it clearly: either approvals must match a standard approved list, or the manager has discretion to approve items outside the standard checklist.
findings.violation: This directly contradicts the Approval Timeline section, which states "The manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list." These cannot both be true.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Employees must keep their equipment in good working condition and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first sentence
findings.violation: This switches from third-person (used throughout the document) to second-person pronouns ("You," "we"), creating an inconsistent voice and tone.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Employees submit the request in the portal and track its status there until payment clears."
findings.violation: This uses second-person pronouns ("you") while the entire document uses third-person perspective ("the employee," "employees"), creating inconsistent voice.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Remove the comma: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility and uploading the receipt."
findings.violation: Grammatically incorrect - a comma should not appear before "and" when joining only two items in a list.

findings.evidence: A section titled "## Overview" states "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period," while the Program Overview section at the start states "The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate Overview section and reconcile the contradictory statements about publication schedule and responsible office.
findings.violation: Duplicate section heading; contradictory information about who publishes the reimbursement log and when it is published.
